lessons.title: States and Parts: Pseudo-classes and Pseudo-elements

objectives.cognitive: Tell a pseudo-class from a pseudo-element and say what :hover, :first-child and ::first-letter pick.
objectives.affective: Value pages that respond clearly to every visitor.
objectives.psychomotor: Highlight Juan's first skill and capitalise his badges' first letters in CodeShare.

blocks.markdown: **How to use this module:** Work in order, Monday to Friday. Run every sample unchanged first, then do its small task. Answer each day's exit slip after its last step.

**Everything happens in CodeShare.** Open your class, then **Module**, this week and a step. **Work in code editor** loads the step's sample files into the editor tabs; **Run code** shows the step's run page in the page window and checks it, and its links open the project's other pages there. It works online and from the classroom laptop; no internet, installation, download or account is needed.

**Reading the outputs:** an output box shows the page text CodeShare checks for the step's run page: the Tab title, the Visible page text, then, on Steps 1, 4, 5, 8 and 9, Media checks. Hover, focus and the other states are not page text, and neither is text added with ::before or ::after. text-transform changes letters, also on ::first-letter. Spaces count.

**Where we start:** Juan's finished Week 7 site (three pages and styles.css) carries forward in your module project. Each step loads its run page and every file it needs; boxes show only new or changed lines.
**Week 8 starts here:** Juan's site has a gallery and a sticky nav, but apart from the links' Week 6 colours nothing reacts when the mouse or the keyboard reaches it.

A pseudo-class, written after one colon, picks elements in a state or a place: :hover under the mouse, :focus where the keyboard or a click is, :first-child the first of its siblings. A pseudo-element, written after two colons, styles a part of an element or adds one: ::first-letter its first letter, ::before and ::after a short text before or after its words, given by content.

A class line-up: "the first in line" is whoever stands at the front, and it changes when someone new arrives (a pseudo-class); the big first letter of a name on a certificate is part of the same name (a pseudo-element).

rows: a whole element in a state or a place
a part of an element, or a new part before or after its words
only when its rule changes letters or hides words
cannot select it; the badge itself reads none

blocks.markdown: **Media steps:** Steps 1, 4, 5, 8 and 9 run index.html, with Juan's picture, sound, video and gallery pictures, files your teacher adds under Media files. Online, CodeShare checks them automatically; Run code waits on Loading media… until they are on this device. Offline, these five steps show Checked by your teacher for now, and your teacher presses Mark done. Steps 2, 3, 6 and 7 run projects.html or contact.html and are checked automatically.

blocks.instruction: Juan's Week 7 site carries forward. A pseudo-class picks elements in a state or a place, written after one colon. .skills li:hover gives a skill a light yellow background while the mouse is over it; .skills li:first-child picks only the first skill, Juan's best, and makes it bold capitals. Run index.html unchanged.

blocks.markdown: **Practice: what does the page check read?** (a) .skills li:hover; (b) .skills li:first-child's text-transform; (c) .badge::first-letter; (d) the badge's own text-transform in Step 2. Answers: (a) nothing: it matches no element without a mouse; (b) uppercase; (c) a page check cannot pick a pseudo-element; (d) none.

**What a page check cannot read:** a page check has no mouse and no keyboard, so :hover, :focus and :focus-visible match nothing in it: you test them yourself in the page window. It cannot pick ::before, ::after or ::first-letter either; the output shows a first letter's text-transform. ::first-line follows where the line wraps, which changes with the window's size, so this module never uses it.
Answer the Monday exit slip now.

lessons.title: Hover and Focus: Links, Buttons, Form Boxes and Lists

objectives.cognitive: Explain :hover, :focus, :focus-visible, :required and :nth-child(), and why focus must be as easy to see as hover.
objectives.affective: Appreciate visitors who use only the keyboard.
objectives.psychomotor: Give Juan's form, button, links and goals their states and test them with the mouse and the Tab key.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Juan's first skill stands out and each badge has one capital, but his form, button and goals look the same whatever you do.

blocks.term: States of links, buttons, form boxes and lists
blocks.markdown: :hover needs a mouse, so give every link and button :focus too, just as easy to see; :focus-visible shows an outline when the keyboard reaches a link. :required picks boxes that must be filled, :nth-child(odd) the 1st, 3rd, 5th items. Page checks read these structural and form pseudo-classes, never hover or focus: a check has no mouse or keyboard.
An elevator button lights up when it is pressed with a finger or reached any other way; a good page lights up a link for the mouse and for the keyboard alike.

rows: the box, button or link a click or Tab reached
focus the browser shows, as with the Tab key

blocks.instruction: Pseudo-classes on a form. input:required gives every box that must be filled a maroon border. The box you click or Tab into gets a 3px maroon outline with :focus, and the button turns white on maroon with button:hover and button:focus, so the keyboard sees what the mouse sees. Run contact.html unchanged.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Juan's links, button and form boxes react to the mouse and the keyboard, but his lists and paragraphs have no decorations.

That text is decoration: it is not page text, and some screen readers skip it, so every word a visitor needs stays in the HTML. ::first-letter styles the first letter, as a large floated drop cap or with text-transform, which does change the page text.
A greeting card: the printed stars around the message are decoration; the message is what you read aloud.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Browsers show no error for a broken selector: one wrong letter or one space can switch a whole rule off.

rows.see: A rule does nothing: its words keep their old letters, and no error shows.
rows.means: A pseudo-class or pseudo-element is misspelt (:frist-child, ::frist-letter).

rows.see: A rule with several selectors does nothing at all.
rows.means: One selector in the comma list is invalid, so the whole rule is dropped.
rows.fix: Repair or remove the bad selector.

rows.means: The space means inside: it looks for a first child inside each li.
rows.fix: No space before the colon: li:first-child.

rows.see: A badge loses its capital first letter after you add ::before.
rows.means: The ::before text comes first, so ::first-letter styles its first character.
rows.fix: Put the symbol in ::after, or leave it out.

rows.see: The symbol does not show, and the next line of the rule does nothing.
rows.means: content's closing quote is missing: the browser skips that line and the next one.

rows.see: Something reacts to the mouse but not to the Tab key.
rows.fix: Add :focus to the same rule: a:hover, a:focus.

performanceTask.title: My Resume, Week 8: Hover, Focus and a Pseudo-element
performanceTask.markdown:
Start Thursday; finish and present Friday. In CodeShare open Projects, then Personal performance-task project. Your Week 7 site carries forward: add this week's rules to your own styles.css.

Give your links and skill items a hover state, and give every link and button a focus state that is as easy to see as hover: the same colours for :focus, and a :focus-visible outline. Add one structural pseudo-class, such as :first-child on your skills, and at least one pseudo-element: a short symbol with ::before or ::after (content in quotes), or a ::first-letter drop cap. Text added with content is decoration: it is not page text and some screen readers skip it, so keep every word a visitor needs in the HTML. Test with the mouse and with the Tab key in the page window. Hover, focus and pseudo-elements work the same online and offline; offline your gallery pictures still show only their alt text until you add them online.

Use only safe details: no home address, phone number, birth date, ID numbers or personal social-media accounts, and no other people in any picture. Run code until index.html runs with no error, then press Submit this version. Saving or running is not submitting.

Thursday: 0–60 minutes, repairs and the Thursday strip; 60–120 minutes, plan on paper, show the teacher, then start. Friday: 0–30 minutes, finish and run; 30–105 minutes, five-minute presentations; 105–120 minutes, Friday strip and Submit this version.
checklist: Keep your Week 7 site: every page, the nav bar, the gallery and styles.css linked from every page.
A hover state on your links and skill items, with colours from the chart (4.5:1 or more).
Focus as easy to see as hover: :focus in the same rule as :hover, and a :focus-visible outline (3:1 or more).
One structural pseudo-class on a list, such as :first-child, :last-child or :nth-child(odd).
At least one pseudo-element: ::before or ::after with a short symbol in quotes, or a ::first-letter drop cap.
Every word a visitor needs is in the HTML, not in content.
Nothing in url(); no address, phone, birth date, ID numbers, social media or other people in a picture.
Run code shows no error; the mouse and the Tab key both show your states; press Submit this version, then present.
